photos.title: Full Display
photos.story: Every feather up and fanned, the national bird doing the one thing it's known for — a rare burst of colour against the dry scrub of Rajasthan.

photos.title: Two Generations
photos.story: A juvenile keeps close to an adult on the same stretch of marsh where this whole project began — the tallest flying bird in the world, dwarfing everything around it.
photos.credit: Rohit Sharma / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

photos.title: Two of a Kind
photos.story: A pair paused mid-conversation on an old sandstone marker, the morning mist folding the grassland behind them into a single soft wash of colour.

photos.title: Salt and Pink
photos.story: Thousands gather on the white salt flats every winter, turning the horizon a colour that doesn't belong to the desert around it.
photos.credit: Prof Ranga Sai / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

photos.title: Full Yawn
photos.story: Mid-morning heat, and the biggest cat in the reserve makes no effort to hide how unimpressed it is with all of it.
photos.credit: Rohit Sharma / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

photos.title: Mirror Water
photos.story: A still grey morning, a still grey lake, and one long orange bill breaking the symmetry.

photos.title: Last Light on the Wetland
photos.story: As the sun dropped below the tree line, the whole lake turned to amber. One quiet ripple was all that gave the bird away.

photos.title: The Wetland Itself
photos.story: Before any bird lands in frame, this is the place — flooded grassland and still water, the whole reason the park exists.

photos.title: Two in the Canopy
photos.story: Two half-grown chicks stand shoulder to shoulder in a high nest of bare acacia branches, fog rolling through the treetops around them.

photos.title: Blue on Bark
photos.story: It held the same dead branch for twenty minutes, turning only its head, weighing every ripple on the water below.

photos.title: Held Ground
photos.story: Coiled into dry grass the colour of its own scales, this python took the better part of an hour to notice — or to admit it had been seen.

photos.title: Held Stare
photos.story: It crossed the track without hurrying, gave the vehicles one long look, and kept walking into the sal forest.
photos.credit: Bernard Gagnon / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

photos.title: Dunes at Dusk
photos.story: A few hours west of the wetlands, the same state turns to sand — the light doing the same slow amber trick it does over water.
photos.credit: Sankara Subramanian / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

photos.title: Neighbours
photos.story: Coots and a shoveler kept their distance in the reeds while the stork held the shoreline alone.

photos.title: On the Move
photos.story: Muscle rolling under patterned scale, the python eases down a sunlit bank toward cover.

photos.title: Talons and Catch
photos.story: Chestnut and white against bare bark, pausing just long enough over a fresh catch to be seen.

photos.title: Green on Green
photos.story: A carpet of duckweed turned the entire wetland the same colour as the bird standing in it.
